args.CodeContent:
#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# Fix GRUB "file '/@/boot/grub/grubenv' not found" error on btrfs
# and enable GRUB to remember the last booted OS
#
# Root cause: btrfs is a copy-on-write filesystem. GRUB cannot write to
# grubenv on btrfs (save_env fails). The previous fix used a symlink to the
# EFI partition, but GRUB's btrfs driver can't follow cross-filesystem symlinks.
#
# Solution: 
# 1. Create a real grubenv on btrfs (so load_env in 00_header doesn't error)
# 2. Create grubenv on EFI partition (FAT32, where GRUB CAN write)
# 3. Add a custom GRUB script that loads env from EFI and redefines
#    savedefault() to save to EFI instead of btrfs
# 4. Post-process grub.cfg to redirect remaining save_env calls to EFI
#
# Run with: sudo bash /home/ahmad/antigravity/fix_grub_savedefault.sh
# =============================================================================

set -e

# Must be root
if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Run with sudo"
    exit 1
fi

# Check EFI partition
if ! mountpoint -q /boot/efi; then
    echo "ERROR: /boot/efi is not mounted"
    exit 1
fi

# --- Configuration ---
EFI_UUID="2404-3B7C"  # From blkid /dev/nvme0n1p2
EFI_REL="/EFI/ubuntu"  # Relative path within EFI partition
EFI_DIR="/boot/efi${EFI_REL}"

# Verify EFI dir exists
if [ ! -d "$EFI_DIR" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: EFI GRUB directory $EFI_DIR not found"
    echo "Available dirs:"
    ls /boot/efi/EFI/ 2>/dev/null || echo "  (permission denied)"
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== GRUB btrfs grubenv fix ==="
echo "EFI partition: /dev/nvme0n1p2 (UUID: $EFI_UUID, FAT32)"
echo "EFI GRUB dir:  $EFI_DIR"
echo ""

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: Create proper grubenv files
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[1/5] Creating grubenv files..."

# Remove the broken symlink
rm -f /boot/grub/grubenv

# Create a real grubenv on btrfs (1024-byte fixed-size file)
# This prevents the "file not found" error from 00_header's load_env
grub-editenv /boot/grub/grubenv create
echo "  ✓ /boot/grub/grubenv (btrfs - for load_env compatibility)"

# Create grubenv on EFI partition (FAT32 - GRUB can write here)
grub-editenv "$EFI_DIR/grubenv" create
echo "  ✓ $EFI_DIR/grubenv (FAT32 - for save_env)"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: Create early GRUB script to search for EFI partition
# This runs BEFORE 00_header, making $btrfs_efi_part available
# for any save_env calls in 00_header's generated code
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[2/5] Creating EFI partition search script (00_0_btrfs_efi)..."

cat > /etc/grub.d/00_0_btrfs_efi << 'EOFSCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
# Auto-generated by fix_grub_savedefault.sh
# Searches for the EFI partition early so $btrfs_efi_part is available
# for save_env -f calls throughout grub.cfg
EOFSCRIPT

# Append the GRUB code with variables expanded
cat >> /etc/grub.d/00_0_btrfs_efi << EOFSCRIPT
cat << 'GRUBEOF'
# --- btrfs fix: locate EFI partition for grubenv ---
search --no-floppy --fs-uuid --set=btrfs_efi_part ${EFI_UUID}
GRUBEOF
EOFSCRIPT

chmod +x /etc/grub.d/00_0_btrfs_efi

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: Create GRUB script that loads env from EFI and overrides
# savedefault() to save to EFI instead of btrfs
# This runs AFTER 00_header, overriding its stale btrfs values
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[3/5] Creating env override script (01_btrfs_env_fix)..."

cat > /etc/grub.d/01_btrfs_env_fix << 'EOFSCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
# Auto-generated by fix_grub_savedefault.sh
# Loads grubenv from EFI partition (overrides 00_header's btrfs load)
# and redefines savedefault() to save to EFI
EOFSCRIPT

# Append GRUB code - use unquoted heredoc so EFI_UUID/EFI_REL expand
cat >> /etc/grub.d/01_btrfs_env_fix << EOFSCRIPT
cat << 'GRUBEOF'
# --- btrfs fix: load env from EFI partition (FAT32) ---
if [ -s (\$btrfs_efi_part)${EFI_REL}/grubenv ]; then
  load_env -f (\$btrfs_efi_part)${EFI_REL}/grubenv
  set have_grubenv=true
fi

# Override savedefault to save to EFI instead of btrfs
function savedefault {
  if [ -z "\${boot_once}" ]; then
    saved_entry="\${chosen}"
    save_env -f (\$btrfs_efi_part)${EFI_REL}/grubenv saved_entry
  fi
}
GRUBEOF
EOFSCRIPT

chmod +x /etc/grub.d/01_btrfs_env_fix

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 4: Create post-processing script for remaining save_env calls
# The savedefault function handles 'save_env saved_entry' but there are
# other direct save_env calls in 00_header (prev_entry, next_entry, etc.)
# that also need redirecting to EFI
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[4/5] Creating grub.cfg post-processor..."

cat > /usr/local/bin/grub-btrfs-postprocess << 'EOFPOST'
#!/bin/bash
# Post-process grub.cfg to redirect remaining save_env calls to EFI partition
# Auto-generated by fix_grub_savedefault.sh
EOFPOST

cat >> /usr/local/bin/grub-btrfs-postprocess << EOFPOST
GRUBCFG="/boot/grub/grub.cfg"
EFI_PATH="${EFI_REL}/grubenv"

if [ ! -f "\$GRUBCFG" ]; then
    echo "grub-btrfs-postprocess: \$GRUBCFG not found, skipping"
    exit 0
fi

# Redirect save_env calls that don't already use -f flag
# These are direct save_env calls from 00_header (prev_entry, next_entry, etc.)
# Note: savedefault function is already overridden by 01_btrfs_env_fix
sed -i '/save_env -f/!{s|save_env prev_entry|save_env -f (\$btrfs_efi_part)'"${EFI_REL}"'/grubenv prev_entry|g}' "\$GRUBCFG"
sed -i '/save_env -f/!{s|save_env next_entry|save_env -f (\$btrfs_efi_part)'"${EFI_REL}"'/grubenv next_entry|g}' "\$GRUBCFG"
sed -i '/save_env -f/!{s|save_env prev_saved_entry|save_env -f (\$btrfs_efi_part)'"${EFI_REL}"'/grubenv prev_saved_entry|g}' "\$GRUBCFG"
sed -i '/save_env -f/!{s|save_env saved_entry|save_env -f (\$btrfs_efi_part)'"${EFI_REL}"'/grubenv saved_entry|g}' "\$GRUBCFG"
sed -i '/save_env -f/!{s|save_env initrdfail|save_env -f (\$btrfs_efi_part)'"${EFI_REL}"'/grubenv initrdfail|g}' "\$GRUBCFG"

echo "grub-btrfs-postprocess: grub.cfg patched for btrfs save_env"
EOFPOST

chmod +x /usr/local/bin/grub-btrfs-postprocess

# Create kernel postinst hook so post-processing runs after kernel updates
mkdir -p /etc/kernel/postinst.d
cat > /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-grub-btrfs-fix << 'HOOK'
#!/bin/bash
# Auto-run grub-btrfs-postprocess after kernel updates
[ -x /usr/local/bin/grub-btrfs-postprocess ] && /usr/local/bin/grub-btrfs-postprocess
HOOK
chmod +x /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-grub-btrfs-fix

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 5: Regenerate grub.cfg and post-process
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[5/5] Running update-grub + post-processing..."
update-grub 2>&1
/usr/local/bin/grub-btrfs-postprocess

echo ""
echo "=== Done! ==="
echo ""
echo "What was fixed:"
echo "  ✓ 'file /@/boot/grub/grubenv not found' error — gone"
echo "  ✓ GRUB will remember your last OS choice (saved to EFI partition)"
echo "  ✓ Kernel update hook installed (auto-patches after updates)"
echo ""
echo "Files created:"
echo "  /boot/grub/grubenv                       — real file (not symlink)"
echo "  $EFI_DIR/grubenv              — writable grubenv on FAT32"
echo "  /etc/grub.d/00_0_btrfs_efi                — EFI partition search"
echo "  /etc/grub.d/01_btrfs_env_fix               — env load + savedefault override"
echo "  /usr/local/bin/grub-btrfs-postprocess       — save_env patcher"
echo "  /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-grub-btrfs-fix   — auto-runs after kernel updates"
echo ""
echo "Note: If you manually run 'sudo update-grub', also run:"
echo "  sudo grub-btrfs-postprocess"
